About these docs

The licence, the alpha status, what these pages cover and how they are checked, how to see which release they describe and how to report a problem.

Published 2026-11-04 · Updated 2026-11-04

1. Licence #

qargi is released under the MIT licence. The text is in the LICENSE file of the repository. The licence applies to the tool and to these pages.

2. Status #

qargi is alpha. It is versioned with Semantic Versioning and is below 1.0, so a command, an option or a file format can change in any release. The releases page lists every change, and the Changed and Removed sections are the ones to read before you update. Expect rough edges and report them.

3. What is here and what is not #

  • The pages written by hand cover the work of a lead: install, set up, the daily loop, dispatching and verifying a task, and safety.
  • The command reference is generated from the same description that qargi help and man qargi print, for the release named in the header and footer of every page.
  • The releases page is generated from the changelog.
  • The README in the repository is the overview, and man qargi is the complete manual. These pages do not repeat them.

4. How the pages are checked #

Every qargi command and option that a page names is looked up in the command description of the release. Links and anchors must resolve. A page that names a command that does not exist, or a private name from the list of forbidden words, fails the build and is not published. The check proves that a command exists and takes that option; it does not prove that the advice is right for your project, so read the plan a command prints before you apply it.

The examples use these names: the project myproject, the members forge, scribe and reader, and the run slug rename-verb. Words in capitals such as NAME, RUN and TOKEN stand for a value you supply.

5. Which release a page describes #

The header and the footer of each page name the release it was checked against. When the hand pages are ahead of a release the stamp says so. If you run an older qargi than the stamp, qargi version tells you which one you have, and the releases page tells you what differs.

6. Report a problem #

Open an issue at github.com/rett/qargi/issues. Say which page, what you typed or read, what you expected and what happened, and the output of qargi version. For a problem with a command, include its exit status and the message. Do not paste tokens, credentials or private paths.
